label: 802.1x Wireless
description: IEEE 802.1X authenticated wireless access provides secure network connectivity using enterprise-grade authentication methods. This service supports WPA2-Enterprise and WPA3-Enterprise security with EAP-TLS (certificate-based), PEAP-MSCHAPv2 (username/password), TEAP, and other EAP methods. The Windows WLAN AutoConfig service (WLANSVC) manages wireless connections, scanning, authentication, and roaming. Proper configuration requires coordination between Windows clients, wireless access points/controllers, RADIUS servers (NPS or third-party), and certificate infrastructure for EAP-TLS deployments.

l1: What Windows version is the wireless client running? (Run: [System.Environment]::OSVersion.Version; Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select Caption,Version,BuildNumber)
What is the exact symptom — cannot associate to the SSID, associates but authentication fails (802.1x), connects but gets no IP, assigned to wrong VLAN, or keeps disconnecting after successful auth?
Is this affecting all wireless clients on the SSID, or specific client models, OS versions, or user accounts?
What wireless infrastructure is in use — Cisco WLC/Catalyst Center, Meraki, Aruba Central/AOS, Ruckus SmartZone, Ubiquiti UniFi, or HPE Aruba Instant?
What SSID security type is affected — WPA2-Enterprise (AES), WPA3-Enterprise (AES-256-GCM/CCMP), WPA3-Enterprise 192-bit, or WPA2-Personal?
Is NPS the RADIUS backend, or is a third-party RADIUS server in use (Cisco ISE, Aruba ClearPass, FreeRADIUS, FortiAuthenticator)?
What EAP method is configured — EAP-TLS (certificate), PEAP-MSCHAPv2 (username/password), PEAP-TLS, TEAP, or TTLS?
Is the Wireless AutoConfig service (WLANSVC) running on the client? (Run: Get-Service WLANSVC | Select Name,Status,StartType,DisplayName)
When did this start — WAP controller firmware update, TLS certificate expiry, SSID security policy change, GPO change, or NPS server change?

Is Windows Credential Guard enabled? (Run: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_DeviceGuard -Namespace root\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard | Select SecurityServicesConfigured) — Note: MSCHAPv2 cannot work with Credential Guard enabled.
l2: Is the wireless profile deployed via Group Policy as a Computer Configuration (Wireless Network IEEE 802.11) policy or User Configuration policy? (Run: gpresult /r | Select-String -Pattern 'Wireless|WLAN|802.11')

Does the profile use machine authentication only, user authentication only, or machine-then-user (Machine or User authentication mode)? (Run: netsh wlan show profile name='<SSID>' key=clear | Select-String -Pattern 'authMode')
Is the WAP controller/AP configured with the correct NPS RADIUS server IPs (primary and secondary) on UDP 1812 — and the correct shared secret?

What radio band and channel is the client associating on — 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, or 6 GHz (Wi-Fi 6E)? Is band steering forcing clients to a band where authentication fails? (Run: netsh wlan show interfaces)
Is PMK (Pairwise Master Key) caching or OKC (Opportunistic Key Caching) enabled on the controller — could stale PMK entries cause re-authentication failures during roaming?

Is 802.11r Fast Transition (FT) or 802.11v BSS Transition Management configured — could FT-EAP be failing for clients that do not support it? (Run: Get-NetAdapter | Where InterfaceDescription -like '*wireless*' | Select Name,DriverVersion)
What NAS-Port-Type value is the WAP controller sending in RADIUS Access-Requests — Wireless (value 19) or IEEE 802.11 (value 5)? Does the NPS Network Policy condition match?
Is the RADIUS server timeout on the WAP controller sufficient for EAP-TLS multi-round-trip exchanges — minimum 10-15 seconds for EAP-TLS with OCSP checking?
Is there a RADIUS Dead Server Detection or failover mechanism on the WAP — is the secondary NPS server reachable and configured correctly?
For WPA3-Enterprise deployments: Does the wireless adapter driver support WPA3-Enterprise? (Run: netsh wlan show drivers | Select-String -Pattern 'WPA3|192-bit')

For certificate-based authentication: Are client certificates enrolled with correct EKU (Extended Key Usage) — Client Authentication (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2) for machine auth, Smart Card Logon (1.3.6.1.4.1.311.20.2.2) for user auth? (Run: certutil -store My | Select-String -Pattern 'EKU')

l1: Run 'Get-Service WLANSVC | Select Name,Status,StartType,DisplayName' — is Wireless AutoConfig service running and set to automatic startup?
Run 'netsh wlan show profiles' — is the correct enterprise SSID profile present on the client?
Run 'netsh wlan show profile name="<SSID>" key=clear' — share the full profile output including authentication mode, EAP type, and cipher settings.

Run 'netsh wlan show interfaces' — share the current association SSID, BSSID, signal quality, authentication algorithm (WPA2/WPA3), cipher (AES/AES-256), and state (Connected/Authenticating/Disconnected).

Check Security event log for Event ID 5632 (802.1x auth started) and 5633 (802.1x auth failed) — share the error code and reason from Event 5633. (Run: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=5632 or EventID=5633)]]" | Select TimeCreated,Id,Message | Format-List)
On the WAP controller: check the client authentication and association log for the failing client MAC — what stage does authentication fail at (association, 802.1x EAP exchange, RADIUS response)?
Does the client receive an IP address after association? ('ipconfig /all') — if yes, 802.1x auth succeeded and the issue is DHCP/VLAN assignment; if no, auth itself failed.

Run 'Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-WLAN-AutoConfig/Operational -MaxEvents 20 | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,Message' — check for WLAN AutoConfig operational events indicating association state transitions.
l2: Capture wireless 802.1x ETL trace: 'netsh trace start capture=yes provider=Microsoft-Windows-WLAN-AutoConfig level=5 keywords=0xFFFFFFFF tracefile=C:\wlan_8021x.etl' — reproduce the issue — run 'netsh trace stop' — convert with 'netsh trace convert C:\wlan_8021x.etl'

Run 'Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-WLAN-AutoConfig/Operational | Sort TimeCreated -Descending | Select -First 50 | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,Message' — look for EAP method negotiation (event 8001/8002), roaming events, and authentication failures.

On NPS: filter Security event log for Event ID 6273 (auth failure) and 6272 (auth success) — match the Calling-Station-Id attribute to the client's MAC address (format: XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX or XXXXXXXXXXXX depending on vendor). (Run: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6272 or EventID=6273)]]" | Format-List)

Run 'certutil -store My' (machine cert store) and 'certutil -store -user My' (user cert store) — verify subject, expiry date, issuer chain, and EKU (Extended Key Usage) includes Client Authentication (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2).
Run 'gpresult /r | Select-String -Pattern "Wireless|WLAN|802.11"' — confirm Wireless Network (IEEE 802.11) policy is in Applied GPOs for Computer or User configuration.

On the WAP controller: run 'debug client <MAC>' or equivalent vendor command (Cisco: 'debug client <MAC>', Aruba: 'show ap client-spectrum <MAC>', Meraki: check client event log) — capture the full RADIUS exchange (Access-Request, Access-Challenge ×N, Access-Accept/Reject).
Run 'netsh wlan show drivers' — share NIC driver version, radio type (802.11n/ac/ax/be), supported authentication types (WPA2-Enterprise, WPA3-Enterprise), and supported cipher suites.
Run 'netsh wlan show networks mode=bssid' — share the security type, authentication, cipher, and BSSID information visible for the target SSID.
Verify NPS RADIUS client registration for the WAP controller IP: 'netsh nps show client' — confirm IP address, shared secret hash, and vendor-specific attributes.
Run 'Get-NetAdapter | Where InterfaceDescription -like "*wireless*" | Select Name,Status,DriverVersion,DriverDate,InterfaceDescription,LinkSpeed' — check driver version and link speed capabilities.

For roaming issues: Run 'Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-WLAN-AutoConfig/Operational | Where Message -like "*roam*" | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,Message' — check for roam initiation, BSS transition, and re-authentication events.

For WPA3-Enterprise: Verify the wireless profile authentication value is 'WPA3ENT' or 'WPA3ENT192' (Run: netsh wlan show profile name='<SSID>' key=clear | Select-String -Pattern 'authentication'), and check if driver supports WPA3 (netsh wlan show drivers).

Check for Credential Guard interference: Run 'Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_DeviceGuard -Namespace root\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard | Select SecurityServicesConfigured' — if enabled, PEAP-MSCHAPv2 will fail; switch to EAP-TLS or disable Credential Guard.

l1: Restart Wireless AutoConfig service: 'Restart-Service WLANSVC -Force' — wait 10 seconds — verify service is running ('Get-Service WLANSVC') — retry connection.

Delete and recreate the wireless profile: 'netsh wlan delete profile name="<SSID>"' — force GPO reapplication with 'gpupdate /force /target:computer' or manually reconfigure via Settings > Network & Internet > WiFi.

Verify machine certificate is enrolled, valid, and not expired: Open certlm.msc > Personal > Certificates — check Valid To date, issuer chain, and EKU includes Client Authentication (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2).
Check NPS Network Policy conditions — confirm the machine or user account is in the required Windows Group condition (e.g., 'Domain Computers' for machine auth, 'Wireless Users' for user auth).
Verify RADIUS shared secret is identical on NPS and the WAP controller — check for trailing whitespace in shared secret fields (common cause of authentication failures).

If using PEAP-MSCHAPv2: confirm user's AD password has not expired — 'Get-ADUser <user> -Properties PasswordExpired,PasswordLastSet | Select PasswordExpired,PasswordLastSet' — expired passwords cause auth failures.

Check if Windows Credential Guard is enabled — 'Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_DeviceGuard -Namespace root\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard | Select SecurityServicesConfigured' — if enabled, PEAP-MSCHAPv2 will not work; switch to EAP-TLS or disable Credential Guard.
Verify wireless adapter driver is current — visit OEM website (Intel, Realtek, Broadcom, Qualcomm) to download latest driver supporting WPA2-Enterprise/WPA3-Enterprise.
l2: For EAP-TLS certificate trust issues: push issuing CA root certificate to all clients via GPO — 'Computer Configuration > Policies > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Public Key Policies > Trusted Root Certification Authorities' — also deploy intermediate CA certificates.

For PEAP server certificate not trusted by clients: in the wireless profile (GPO or manual), under Authentication > PEAP Properties, ensure the NPS server certificate issuer root CA is listed under 'Trusted Root Certification Authorities' — validate server certificate has 'Server Authentication' EKU (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1).

For roaming re-authentication failures: enable OKC (Opportunistic Key Caching) on the WAP controller — confirm client profile has PMK caching enabled (PMKCacheMode=enabled, PMKCacheTTL=720 minutes) and 'Single Sign On' disabled to avoid forced re-auth on roam.

For machine-then-user auth failure: confirm machine authenticates at boot (using machine cert / machine credentials) before user logon — GPO Wireless Network profile > Security > Authentication Mode = 'User or Machine authentication' — verify machine certificate is in Local Computer store, not User store.

For RADIUS timeout causing auth failure: on the WAP controller, set the RADIUS authentication timeout to 15-30 seconds — EAP-TLS with OCSP/CRL checking can take 5-10 seconds per round-trip; increase to 30-45 seconds if CRL distribution points are slow.

For NAS-Port-Type mismatch in NPS policy: capture a RADIUS packet (Wireshark on NPS server, filter 'radius') — confirm the exact NAS-Port-Type value sent by the WAP (Wireless=19, IEEE 802.11=5, Ethernet=15) — update NPS Network Policy condition to match.

For 802.11r Fast Transition (FT) causing EAP-TLS failure: disable FT on the SSID (test environment first) — some Windows clients or older wireless drivers do not fully support FT-EAP mode; verify driver supports 802.11r (netsh wlan show drivers).

For WPA3-Enterprise 192-bit mode certificate issues: verify all certificates (root CA, issuing CA, client certs) meet strict WPA3-Enterprise 192-bit requirements — minimum RSA 3072-bit or ECC P-384, SHA-384 hashing, no MD5/SHA-1 signatures.

Analyze WLAN AutoConfig ETL trace with Message Analyzer or Text Analysis Tool (TAT): look for EAP method negotiation (WLAN-AutoConfig event 8001/8002), TLS Alert Codes (40=handshake_failure, 42=bad_certificate, 44=certificate_revoked, 46=certificate_unknown, 48=unknown_ca), and association state machine transitions.

For WAP controller integration issues: verify RADIUS CoA (Change of Authorization) and Dynamic VLAN assignment are configured correctly on the WAP — check that the WAP can interpret RADIUS attributes like Tunnel-Private-Group-ID (VLAN ID) and Filter-Id.

For intermittent auth failures: check for time synchronization issues between client, NPS, and CA — run 'w32tm /query /status' on all systems — Kerberos and certificate validation require accurate time (within 5 minutes skew).

For client-specific failures: check wireless adapter power management settings — Device Manager > Network Adapters > Wireless Adapter > Power Management > uncheck 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power' — power saving can cause authentication timeouts.

l1: Run 'netsh wlan show profiles > C:\wlan_profiles.txt' — capture all wireless profiles including enterprise SSIDs.
Run 'netsh wlan show interfaces > C:\wlan_interfaces.txt' — capture current wireless adapter state, SSID, BSSID, authentication, cipher, and signal quality.
Export Security event log: 'wevtutil epl Security C:\Security_Events_Client.evtx' — includes Event IDs 5632, 5633 (802.1x auth), 6272, 6273 (NPS auth if NPS is local).
Run 'netsh wlan show drivers > C:\wlan_drivers.txt' — capture wireless adapter driver version, radio type, and supported authentication/cipher types.
Run 'Get-Service WLANSVC | Select Name,Status,StartType,DisplayName > C:\wlansvc_status.txt' — capture WLAN AutoConfig service status.
Run 'Get-NetAdapter | Where InterfaceDescription -like "*wireless*" | Select Name,Status,DriverVersion,DriverDate,InterfaceDescription,LinkSpeed | Format-List > C:\wireless_adapter_info.txt'
l2: Capture WLAN 802.1x trace: 'netsh trace start capture=yes provider=Microsoft-Windows-WLAN-AutoConfig level=5 keywords=0xFFFFFFFF tracefile=C:\wlan_8021x_trace.etl' — reproduce the authentication or roaming issue — run 'netsh trace stop' — convert with 'netsh trace convert C:\wlan_8021x_trace.etl'.

Export WLAN-AutoConfig Operational log: 'wevtutil epl Microsoft-Windows-WLAN-AutoConfig/Operational C:\WLAN_AutoConfig_Operational.evtx' — contains detailed EAP negotiation, roaming, and association events.
Run 'certutil -store My > C:\machine_cert_store.txt' and 'certutil -store -user My > C:\user_cert_store.txt' — capture machine and user certificate stores for EAP-TLS troubleshooting.

Collect WAP controller logs: client association log, RADIUS proxy log, and 802.11 state machine log for the failing client MAC — vendor-specific (Cisco WLC: 'show client detail <MAC>', Aruba: 'show ap client-spectrum <MAC>', Meraki: Dashboard > Monitor > Clients).
Run 'gpresult /h C:\gpo_wireless_report.html' — generate comprehensive GPO report showing applied Wireless Network (IEEE 802.11) policies.
Run 'Get-NetAdapter | Select Name,Status,DriverVersion,DriverDate,InterfaceDescription,LinkSpeed | Out-File C:\nic_info.txt' — capture all network adapter details.
Collect NPS IAS logs and Security event log from the NPS server: 'wevtutil epl Security C:\NPS_Security.evtx' — filter for Event IDs 6272 (auth success) and 6273 (auth failure).

TSS full data collection: '.\TSS.ps1 -Scenario NET_WLAN' — run on the affected client, reproduce the authentication or association failure, stop when prompted — this collects comprehensive WLAN, EAP, and RADIUS traces.

For certificate troubleshooting: Run 'certutil -v -store My > C:\machine_cert_detailed.txt' and 'certutil -v -store -user My > C:\user_cert_detailed.txt' — capture detailed certificate properties including EKU, key usage, and chain.
For roaming issues: Run 'netsh wlan show profiles name="<SSID>" key=clear > C:\ssid_profile_details.txt' — capture PMK caching settings, preAuthMode, and authentication mode.
For WPA3-Enterprise: Run 'netsh wlan show drivers | Select-String -Pattern "WPA3|192-bit" > C:\wpa3_support.txt' — verify driver supports WPA3-Enterprise.

For Credential Guard: Run 'Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_DeviceGuard -Namespace root\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard | Select SecurityServicesConfigured,SecurityServicesRunning > C:\credential_guard_status.txt' — capture Credential Guard status.
Collect CAPI2 event log for certificate operations: 'wevtutil epl CAPI2 C:\CAPI2.evtx' — useful for troubleshooting certificate enrollment and validation issues.
For time synchronization: Run 'w32tm /query /status > C:\time_sync_status.txt' — capture NTP configuration and time skew information.

auth_fails_after_associate.title: Client associates to SSID but 802.1x authentication fails
auth_fails_after_associate.description: This playbook addresses scenarios where Windows clients successfully associate to an enterprise SSID (WPA2-Enterprise or WPA3-Enterprise) but fail during the 802.1X EAP authentication phase. Common causes include RADIUS shared secret mismatches, certificate trust issues (EAP-TLS), Credential Guard interference with PEAP-MSCHAPv2, RADIUS timeout settings, NPS Network Policy condition mismatches, and wireless profile configuration errors. The WLAN AutoConfig service (WLANSVC) manages the EAP exchange with the RADIUS server via the wireless access point controller.

steps.action: Get-Service WLANSVC | Select Name,Status,StartType,DisplayName
steps.expect: Status: Running, StartType: Automatic — service must be running for wireless authentication

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=5632 or EventID=5633)]]" | Select TimeCreated,Id,Message | Format-List
steps.expect: Event 5633 = 802.1x auth failed — note EAP error code and reason string in event message

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6272 or EventID=6273)]]" | Select TimeCreated,Id,Message | Format-List
steps.expect: Event 6273 on NPS server shows Reason Code (e.g., 68=auth method not supported, 65=group mismatch)

steps.action: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_DeviceGuard -Namespace root\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard | Select SecurityServicesConfigured
steps.expect: If Credential Guard enabled, PEAP-MSCHAPv2 will fail — switch to EAP-TLS or disable Credential Guard

steps.action: netsh wlan show profile name='<SSID>' key=clear
steps.expect: EAP type matches what NPS expects — PEAP-MSCHAPv2 (Type 25), EAP-TLS (Type 13), or TEAP (Type 55)

steps.action: netsh nps show client
steps.expect: WAP controller IP registered as RADIUS client with correct shared secret hash

steps.action: On WAP controller: check RADIUS server timeout setting
steps.expect: Timeout at least 15 seconds — EAP-TLS with OCSP/CRL checking requires multiple round trips

steps.action: certutil -store My (machine) and certutil -store -user My (user)
steps.expect: For EAP-TLS: certificates valid, not expired, EKU includes Client Authentication (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2)

steps.action: Get-ADUser <user> -Properties PasswordExpired,PasswordLastSet
steps.expect: For PEAP-MSCHAPv2: PasswordExpired = False — expired passwords cause auth failures

steps.action: netsh wlan delete profile name='<SSID>' then gpupdate /force /target:computer
steps.expect: Profile recreated from GPO with correct EAP settings and authentication mode

steps.action: Verify and re-enter RADIUS shared secret on both NPS and WAP controller
steps.expect: Secrets match exactly including case — check for trailing whitespace

steps.action: Increase RADIUS timeout on WAP controller to 15-30 seconds (30-45s if CRL checking enabled)
steps.expect: EAP-TLS handshake has enough time to complete without timeout

steps.action: For EAP-TLS: Deploy root CA certificate via GPO to Trusted Root Certification Authorities
steps.expect: Clients trust NPS server certificate issuer — prevents 'unknown_ca' TLS alert

steps.action: For PEAP-MSCHAPv2 with Credential Guard: Disable Credential Guard or switch to EAP-TLS
steps.expect: Authentication succeeds — Credential Guard blocks MSCHAPv2 credential usage

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6272)]]" | Select -First 3
steps.expect: Event 6272 = authentication succeeded on NPS server

steps.action: netsh wlan show interfaces
steps.expect: State: Connected, Authentication: WPA2-Enterprise or WPA3-Enterprise, Cipher: AES or AES-256

steps.action: ipconfig /all
steps.expect: Valid IP address received from correct VLAN scope — indicates successful auth and VLAN assignment

roaming_drops.title: Client drops connection when roaming between APs
roaming_drops.description: This playbook addresses roaming failures where Windows clients successfully authenticate to an enterprise SSID but lose connectivity when moving between access points. This is typically caused by 802.11r Fast Transition (FT) incompatibility, disabled PMK caching/OKC (Opportunistic Key Caching), RADIUS timeout issues during re-authentication, or WAP controller misconfiguration. Windows 10/11 supports 802.11r, 802.11k, and 802.11v for fast roaming, but requires driver support and AP-side configuration. When FT is unavailable, Windows falls back to OKC for optimized roaming.

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-WLAN-AutoConfig/Operational | Where Message -like "*roam*" | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,Message
steps.expect: Look for roam initiation events followed by auth failure or disconnection events

steps.action: On WAP controller: check if 802.11r Fast Transition (FT) is enabled on the SSID
steps.expect: FT-EAP may be failing for clients that do not fully support it — some drivers have incomplete FT implementation

steps.action: netsh wlan show drivers | Select-String -Pattern '802.11r|Fast Transition'
steps.expect: Verify wireless driver supports 802.11r — older drivers may not support FT roaming

steps.action: On WAP controller: check PMK caching and OKC settings
steps.expect: If PMK cache entries are stale or OKC is disabled, full re-authentication occurs on every roam causing timeouts

steps.action: Check RADIUS server timeout on WAP controller
steps.expect: If timeout too short (under 15s), full EAP-TLS re-auth during roam times out before completing

steps.action: netsh wlan show profile name='<SSID>' key=clear | Select-String -Pattern 'PMKCacheMode|PMKCacheTTL|preAuthMode'
steps.expect: PMKCacheMode should be 'enabled', PMKCacheTTL typically 720 minutes, preAuthMode 'disabled' for FT compatibility

steps.action: Get-NetAdapter | Where InterfaceDescription -like '*wireless*' | Select Name,DriverVersion
steps.expect: Check driver version — update to latest OEM driver for best roaming support

steps.action: Disable 802.11r Fast Transition on the SSID (test environment first)
steps.expect: Removes FT-EAP requirement — clients fall back to full re-auth or OKC which is more compatible

steps.action: Enable OKC (Opportunistic Key Caching) on WAP controller
steps.expect: OKC allows fast roam without full EAP re-authentication — caches PMK across APs

steps.action: Increase RADIUS timeout on WAP controller to 15-30 seconds
steps.expect: Full re-auth during roam has enough time to complete without timeout

steps.action: Update wireless adapter driver to latest version from OEM (Intel, Realtek, Broadcom)
steps.expect: Latest drivers include improved 802.11r, 802.11k, and 802.11v support for fast roaming

steps.action: Verify PMK caching is enabled in wireless profile: PMKCacheMode=enabled, PMKCacheTTL=720
steps.expect: Client caches PMK locally to speed up re-authentication on roam

steps.action: Walk client between APs and monitor netsh wlan show interfaces continuously
steps.expect: BSSID changes as client roams but State remains Connected throughout — no disconnection or re-auth delays

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-WLAN-AutoConfig/Operational -MaxEvents 50 | Where Message -like "*roam*"
steps.expect: Roam events present without subsequent authentication failure events

steps.action: Continuous ping test during roam: ping -t <gateway_ip>
steps.expect: Ping may drop 1-2 packets during roam but recovers quickly (<2 seconds) — no extended outages

cannot_associate.title: Client cannot associate to enterprise SSID
cannot_associate.description: This playbook addresses scenarios where Windows clients cannot establish a wireless association to an enterprise SSID (WPA2-Enterprise or WPA3-Enterprise). The client may not see the SSID, may fail at the 802.11 association phase, or may not have a valid wireless profile. Common causes include WLAN AutoConfig service issues, missing or incorrect wireless profiles, Group Policy application failures, outdated wireless drivers that don't support WPA3 or newer EAP methods, incorrect SSID security configuration, and hardware compatibility issues.

steps.action: netsh wlan show interfaces
steps.expect: State: Disconnected or Authenticating — not Connected. Check for 'There is no wireless interface on the system' error

steps.action: netsh wlan show networks mode=bssid
steps.expect: Target SSID visible with correct security type WPA2-Enterprise or WPA3-Enterprise. If not visible, check RF coverage and SSID broadcast settings

steps.action: Get-Service WLANSVC | Select Name,Status,StartType,DisplayName
steps.expect: Status: Running, StartType: Automatic — if stopped, wireless functionality is unavailable

steps.action: Get-NetAdapter | Where InterfaceDescription -like '*wireless*' | Select Name,Status
steps.expect: Wireless adapter present and enabled — if disabled, enable via 'Enable-NetAdapter -Name <adapter_name>'

steps.action: netsh wlan show profile name='<SSID>'
steps.expect: Profile present — if missing, GPO has not applied or profile was deleted manually

steps.action: gpresult /r | Select-String -Pattern 'Wireless|WLAN|802.11'
steps.expect: Wireless Network IEEE 802.11 GPO listed in Applied GPOs for Computer or User configuration

steps.action: netsh wlan show drivers
steps.expect: Driver version and supported authentication types — outdated driver may not support WPA3-Enterprise, WPA3-Enterprise 192-bit, or TEAP

steps.action: netsh wlan show drivers | Select-String -Pattern 'WPA3|192-bit|TEAP'
steps.expect: For WPA3-Enterprise deployments: verify driver explicitly supports WPA3 authentication

steps.action: Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select Caption,Version,BuildNumber
steps.expect: Windows 10 1703+ or Windows 11 required for WPA3-Enterprise support

steps.action: Restart-Service WLANSVC -Force
steps.expect: Wireless AutoConfig restarted — retry connection. If service fails to start, check Windows event log for service-specific errors

steps.action: gpupdate /force /target:computer
steps.expect: Wireless profile redeployed from GPO — may require reboot for computer profile application

steps.action: Update wireless NIC driver from OEM website (Intel Driver & Support Assistant, OEM support site)
steps.expect: Driver updated to latest version — supports current authentication types and cipher suites

steps.action: If profile missing: manually create profile via Settings > Network & Internet > WiFi > Manage known networks > Add new network
steps.expect: Profile created with correct SSID, security type (WPA2-Enterprise/WPA3-Enterprise), and EAP method

steps.action: Enable wireless adapter if disabled: Enable-NetAdapter -Name <adapter_name>
steps.expect: Adapter enabled — client can now scan for and associate to wireless networks

steps.action: For WPA3-Enterprise on older Windows: upgrade to Windows 10 1703+ or Windows 11, or downgrade SSID to WPA2-Enterprise
steps.expect: OS/driver compatibility resolved — client can associate to SSID

steps.action: netsh wlan show interfaces
steps.expect: State: Connected, SSID matches target, Authentication: WPA2-Enterprise or WPA3-Enterprise, Cipher: AES or AES-256

steps.action: ipconfig /all
steps.expect: Valid IP address received from correct VLAN scope — indicates successful association, authentication, and DHCP

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6272)]]" | Select -First 1
steps.expect: Event 6272 present on NPS server — confirms successful RADIUS authentication

steps.action: ping -n 4 <gateway_ip>
steps.expect: Successful ping responses — confirms network connectivity after association

wpa3_enterprise_issues.title: WPA3-Enterprise authentication failures
wpa3_enterprise_issues.description: This playbook addresses WPA3-Enterprise and WPA3-Enterprise 192-bit mode authentication issues. WPA3-Enterprise requires Windows 10 1703+ or Windows 11, wireless adapter driver support, and strict certificate requirements. WPA3-Enterprise 192-bit mode imposes very strict certificate requirements including minimum RSA 3072-bit or ECC P-384 keys, SHA-384 hashing, and no MD5/SHA-1 signatures. Common failures include driver incompatibility, certificate non-compliance, and incorrect profile configuration (authentication value must be 'WPA3ENT' or 'WPA3ENT192').

steps.action: Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select Caption,Version,BuildNumber
steps.expect: Windows 10 1703+ (Build 15063) or Windows 11 required for WPA3-Enterprise support

steps.action: netsh wlan show drivers | Select-String -Pattern 'WPA3|192-bit'
steps.expect: Driver explicitly supports WPA3-Enterprise — if not listed, driver or hardware does not support WPA3

steps.action: netsh wlan show profile name='<SSID>' key=clear | Select-String -Pattern 'authentication'
steps.expect: Authentication value must be 'WPA3ENT' for WPA3-Enterprise or 'WPA3ENT192' for 192-bit mode

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=5633)]]" | Select -First 3
steps.expect: Event 5633 error code indicates WPA3-specific failure (e.g., cipher suite mismatch, certificate non-compliance)

steps.action: certutil -v -store My (machine) and certutil -v -store -user My (user)
steps.expect: For WPA3-Enterprise 192-bit: verify RSA >=3072-bit or ECC P-384, SHA-384, no MD5/SHA-1 signatures

steps.action: certutil -store -user My | Select-String -Pattern 'EKU'
steps.expect: EKU includes Client Authentication (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2) — Smart Card Logon EKU also acceptable for user auth

steps.action: On WAP controller: verify SSID security mode is WPA3-Enterprise or WPA3-Enterprise 192-bit
steps.expect: Controller configuration matches client profile expectations — mismatch causes association failures

steps.action: Get-NetAdapter | Where InterfaceDescription -like '*wireless*' | Select Name,DriverVersion
steps.expect: Driver version is recent — older drivers may have incomplete WPA3 implementation

steps.action: Update wireless adapter driver to latest OEM version with WPA3 support
steps.expect: Driver now supports WPA3-Enterprise authentication and cipher suites

steps.action: For WPA3-Enterprise 192-bit: reissue certificates with compliant key sizes (RSA 3072+ or ECC P-384)
steps.expect: Certificates meet WPA3-Enterprise 192-bit strict requirements

steps.action: Recreate wireless profile with correct authentication value: 'WPA3ENT' or 'WPA3ENT192'
steps.expect: Profile configuration matches WAP controller security mode

steps.action: If OS version incompatible: upgrade to Windows 10 1703+ or Windows 11, or downgrade SSID to WPA2-Enterprise
steps.expect: OS/driver compatibility resolved — or fallback to WPA2-Enterprise for older clients

steps.action: Verify root CA certificate chain is complete and deployed to clients via GPO
steps.expect: Clients have full certificate chain including root and intermediate CAs in Trusted Root store

steps.action: netsh wlan show interfaces
steps.expect: State: Connected, Authentication: WPA3-Enterprise or WPA3-Enterprise 192-bit, Cipher: AES-256-GCM or CCMP

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6272)]]" | Select -First 1
steps.expect: Event 6272 present on NPS server — confirms successful WPA3-Enterprise authentication

steps.action: ipconfig /all
steps.expect: Valid IP address received from correct VLAN scope — indicates successful WPA3-Enterprise connection

wap_controller_integration.title: WAP controller and RADIUS integration issues
wap_controller_integration.description: This playbook addresses integration issues between Windows clients, wireless access point controllers (Cisco WLC, Aruba, Meraki, Ruckus, Ubiquiti), and RADIUS servers (NPS, ISE, ClearPass). Common issues include RADIUS shared secret mismatches, NAS-Port-Type attribute mismatches in NPS policies, incorrect RADIUS server IP configuration, Dynamic VLAN assignment failures, RADIUS CoA (Change of Authorization) issues, and timeout misconfigurations. Proper integration requires matching client expectations with controller and RADIUS server configurations.

steps.action: On WAP controller: verify RADIUS server IP addresses (primary and secondary) configured correctly
steps.expect: Primary and secondary NPS/RADIUS server IPs are correct and reachable (test with ping)

steps.action: On WAP controller: verify RADIUS shared secret matches NPS configuration exactly
steps.expect: Shared secret identical on both sides — check for trailing whitespace or case sensitivity

steps.action: On NPS: run 'netsh nps show client' to verify WAP controller IP registration
steps.expect: WAP controller IP is registered as RADIUS client with correct shared secret hash

steps.action: On WAP controller: check RADIUS timeout setting (typically 5-30 seconds)
steps.expect: Timeout sufficient for EAP method — EAP-TLS with OCSP requires 15-30s minimum

steps.action: Capture RADIUS traffic on NPS server with Wireshark (filter: 'radius')
steps.expect: Identify exact NAS-Port-Type value sent by WAP (Wireless=19, IEEE 802.11=5, Ethernet=15)

steps.action: On NPS: check Network Policy conditions for NAS-Port-Type match
steps.expect: NAS-Port-Type condition matches value sent by WAP controller — mismatch causes policy rejection

steps.action: On WAP controller: check Dynamic VLAN assignment configuration (Tunnel-Private-Group-ID)
steps.expect: VLAN assignment attributes configured correctly if using per-user/per-machine VLANs

steps.action: On NPS: check Network Policy for RADIUS standard attributes (Tunnel-Private-Group-ID, Filter-Id)
steps.expect: RADIUS attributes configured in policy match WAP controller expectations

steps.action: Test RADIUS connectivity: 'Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <NPS_IP> -Port 1812'
steps.expect: TCP test succeeds — UDP 1812 may not show as open but connectivity is confirmed

steps.action: Re-enter RADIUS shared secret on both NPS and WAP controller — verify no trailing whitespace
steps.expect: Shared secrets match exactly — authentication attempts no longer fail with shared secret error

steps.action: Update NPS Network Policy NAS-Port-Type condition to match WAP controller value
steps.expect: Policy now matches — RADIUS requests pass condition matching and proceed to authentication

steps.action: Increase RADIUS timeout on WAP controller to 15-30 seconds (30-45s for EAP-TLS with CRL)
steps.expect: Timeout sufficient for complete EAP exchange — no more timeout failures

steps.action: Configure Dynamic VLAN assignment on WAP controller to accept Tunnel-Private-Group-ID attribute
steps.expect: VLAN assignment works correctly — clients placed in appropriate VLANs based on user/group

steps.action: Enable RADIUS Dead Server Detection on WAP controller for failover
steps.expect: Failover to secondary RADIUS server works if primary becomes unavailable

steps.action: For Cisco WLC: verify 'RADIUS Network Access' vs 'RADIUS Accounting' server configuration
steps.expect: Authentication server configured correctly in RADIUS Network Access section

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6272)]]" | Select -First 3
steps.expect: Event 6272 present on NPS server — confirms successful RADIUS authentication

steps.action: netsh wlan show interfaces
steps.expect: State: Connected with correct authentication mode and cipher

steps.action: ipconfig /all
steps.expect: IP address from expected VLAN scope — confirms Dynamic VLAN assignment working

steps.action: On WAP controller: verify client shows in active client list with correct VLAN
steps.expect: Controller shows client associated and authenticated in correct VLAN
